S65.01.needs: a signed-in account and an ordinary website open
S65.01.note: Setup is one consent card, not a multi-step wizard; the code does not show a separate guided flow.
steps: Sign in to AGI in the side panel and open an ordinary website (not a Chrome page or the Web Store).
Click the "Computer Use" tab at the top of the side panel.
Read the card: its headline is "This grants full DevTools-Protocol control" and its title is "Let AGI act on <site>".
Click "Allow browser control on <site>" and accept Chrome's site-access prompt.
Compare with Expected: the card should close and the line "Works on <site>" should appear under the task box.
S65.01.where: Computer Use tab > setup card, after opening an ordinary website: the button "Allow browser control on <site>" (also under Extension settings > Permissions > Grant full browser control)

S65.07.needs: a signed-in account and an ordinary website open
S65.07.note: The code shows screenshot steps as images but does not confirm whether the step list starts open or closed.
steps: Open an ordinary website and sign in to AGI.
Click the "Computer Use" tab, approve the site if asked, type a short task and click "Start".
Click "Assistant steps" to open the step list if it is closed.
Watch the steps appear while AGI works.
Compare with Expected: screenshot steps should show a small picture of the page AGI sees at that moment.
S65.07.where: Computer Use tab > Assistant steps (screenshot entries appear as the task runs)

S65.08.needs: a signed-in account and an approved ordinary website
S65.08.note: The pointer and glow are injected into the page by the run overlay; they appear only while a run is active.
steps: Start a task on an approved ordinary website from the Computer Use tab.
Watch the page while AGI clicks or types.
Compare with Expected: an arrow pointer should move to the place AGI acts, and the page should show a dock with the buttons "Stop" and "Take over" at the bottom.
S65.08.where: On the web page itself during a run: a coloured arrow pointer moves to each click target and a coloured glow frames the page

S65.18.needs: a signed-in account, an approved ordinary website and a second tab
S65.18.note: The code is marked partial: the run keeps going after a tab switch, but the final live check for background screenshots and input was not confirmed.
steps: Start a task on an approved ordinary website from the Computer Use tab.
Switch to a different tab in the same window while the task runs.
Return to the Computer Use tab after a few seconds.
Compare with Expected: Assistant steps should keep growing and the run should not show as cancelled.
S65.18.where: Computer Use tab > Assistant steps keep updating while another tab is in front

labels.text: You started using the page, so AGI stopped acting on it.

S65.19.needs: a signed-in account and an approved ordinary website
S65.19.note: The code hands the page to the person on a real click or key press only when AGI is not in the middle of an action, so the tester should try between steps.
steps: Start a task on an approved ordinary website from the Computer Use tab.
While AGI is still acting, click or type on the task page yourself.
Compare with Expected: AGI should stop acting on the page and the notice above should appear in the side panel.
S65.19.where: Computer Use tab shows the notice "You started using the page, so AGI stopped acting on it." when the person uses the task page

S65.20.needs: a signed-in account and an approved ordinary website
steps: Start a task on an approved ordinary website from the Computer Use tab.
While the task runs, click "Stop" in the Computer Use tab.
Watch the button change to "Stopping…" and then the run end.
Compare with Expected: the run should stop at once and the log should say "You stopped the run."
S65.20.where: Computer Use tab > Stop (also the "Stop" button in the dock on the web page)

S65.23.needs: a signed-in account, an approved ordinary website and a site with a form
S65.23.note: Some sensitive steps are refused outright rather than offered for review (for example a payment), so the tester may see a refusal message instead of a card.
steps: Click the "Computer Use" tab and open the menu "How should AGI act in your browser?" and choose "Ask first".
Start a task on an approved ordinary website that reaches a form or button that changes something.
When the card "Approve action:" appears, read the description before choosing.
Compare with Expected: AGI should wait for "Allow" or "Skip" before it acts.
S65.23.where: Computer Use tab > "How should AGI act in your browser?" menu set to "Ask first", then a card titled "Approve action: <tool>" with "Allow", "Allow for this task" and "Skip"

S65.24.needs: a site that requires sign-in and an outside account (Google) if the site uses one
S65.24.note: The Continue button stays hidden until the run pauses for a hand-over.
steps: Start a task on an approved site that asks for sign-in (use the test account the team gives you).
When AGI pauses for sign-in, read the reason in the side panel and sign in on the page yourself.
Click "Continue" in the Computer Use tab to hand the page back.
Compare with Expected: AGI should carry on with the task from the signed-in page.
S65.24.where: Computer Use tab > the "Sign in required" chip, then the "Take over" button; after signing in, click "Continue"

S65.25.needs: a signed-in account and an approved ordinary website
steps: Start a short task on an approved ordinary website from the Computer Use tab.
Open "Assistant steps" when the run has finished.
Click an action line to expand its detail.
Compare with Expected: each action should have its own line that says what was done and whether it was verified.
S65.25.where: Computer Use tab > Assistant steps (each action line starts with "Completed", "Skipped", "Not verified" or "Result")

labels.text: AGI cannot act on this page. Open an ordinary website.
Chrome does not let extensions read this page at all.

S65.26.note: The same idea also appears for chat page attachments, with a different sentence in src/side_panel.ts.
steps: Sign in and make the active tab a Chrome page such as the Chrome Web Store or chrome://extensions.
Click the "Computer Use" tab.
Read the line under the task box.
Compare with Expected: the line should say AGI cannot act on this page and tell the person to open an ordinary website.
S65.26.where: Computer Use tab > the line under the task box: "AGI cannot act on this page. Open an ordinary website."

S65.28.needs: a signed-in account and an approved ordinary website
S65.28.note: The run-stop message is "Access to this site was withdrawn, so the run was stopped." in src/features/side-panel/computerUsePanel.ts; the removal path revokes browser control too.
steps: Start a task on an approved ordinary website so a run is active.
Click "More" in the side panel, then "Extension settings", and find "Permissions".
Click the × next to the site in the approved sites list.
Return to the side panel and watch the run.
Compare with Expected: the run should stop and the message should say access was withdrawn and to approve the site again in the Computer use tab.
S65.28.where: More > Extension settings > Permissions > the × button next to the site (titled "Remove <site>"); then back in the Computer Use tab
